newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ top 40 share index hits new 2-1/2 year high.
newsitem.headline: NZ top 40 share index hits new 2-1/2 year high.

text.p: New Zealand's top 40 share index, the NZSE-40, rose 3.21 points to a new two-and-a-half year high of 2,251.40 in early trade on Wednesday.
The index has not been at this level since late March 1994, when it was at 2,290.06 and on its way down from a high in February 1994 of 2,444.80.

Brokers said New Zealand equities were well underpinned at present, despite the uncertainty surrounding the outcome of the October 12 general election, the country's first under the new proportional representation system.
"I think it's just the fact that people had re-weighted ahead of the election," said Tim Koller, broker at Hendry Hay McIntosh.

"None of the locals appear to want to lighten their load of New Zealand equities...and from the foreigners, I guess a lot are less perturbed about the election than we may be, due to the fact that a lot of other countries do operate successfully under this form of voting."
The new Mixed Member Proportional electoral system is similar to Germany's and is likely to produce a minority or coalition government.

Neville Todd at County Natwest said offshore investors appeared confident there would not be any radical policy change after the election because of the necessity for parties to work in coalition with each other in order to govern.
"That's the thing that I think the international investor has really focused on -- that you're probably not going to see significant changes to major policy issues," he said.
Todd said the market had a "generally firm tone on it".
"I don't think anyone would have anticipated we'd be doing this well three weeks out from the election," he said.
